_meta.description: 200 response for PUT /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/service-window (MYR-316, CORRECTED by MYR-362) — the owner's 'expected back' entry. Authored here from rest-api.md §7.16 'Response 200' because the telemetry repo ships no fixture for this endpoint (docs/contracts/fixtures/rest/ covers read paths only); replace with the upstream file the moment one exists. THE KEY IS `expectedEndAt` AND IT IS THE OWNER COLUMN: §7.16 echoes what was stored in service_expected_end_at, deliberately NOT the resolved serviceEstimatedEndAt, because 'echoing the resolved value would make a client believe its write had been overruled when it has merely been outranked by Tesla on the next read'. This fixture previously carried a `serviceEstimatedEndAt` key the server has never emitted, which is exactly how MYR-362 shipped: the client's optional property decoded to nil on every save and the owner's date vanished from the sheet. A hand-authored fixture is only evidence to the extent it is the wire. The instant is `time.RFC3339` — seconds precision, no fractional part — matching internal/telemetry/service_window.go formatInstantOrNil. Tesla precedence is a READ concern and shows up on the next §7.0/§7.1 fetch.
